## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $\hbar>0$ and let $\alpha>0$, let
$\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_{\Pi}\subseteq L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb
C^{3})$ be the transverse space with $\varepsilon(k)=\alpha|k|$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]],
let $\Lambda>0$, let $g_{1},\dots,g_{J}\in\mathfrak h$ ($J\ge1$) satisfy
$$\operatorname{supp}g_{j}\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\},\qquad \frac{g_{j}}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h ,$$
let $\eta_{0}\in\mathbb R$ and let $c_{1},\dots,c_{J}\in\mathbb C$ with
$$M:=\sum_{j=1}^{J}c_{j}g_{j}\in\mathfrak h .$$
Fix $\Delta\in\mathbb R$ and define the finite Borel measure
$$\nu_{b}(B):=\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\mathbf 1_{B}\bigl(\varepsilon(k)\bigr) \|M(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k,\qquad K_{t}(x):=\frac{1}{\hbar^{2}t}\Bigl|\int_{0}^{t}e^{ixs/\hbar}\,ds\Bigr|^{2}\ \ (t>0),$$
and the vector-valued function
$$A_{b}(k,t):=-\frac{i\eta_{0}}{\hbar}M(k)\int_{0}^{t} e^{i(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta)s/\hbar}\,ds\qquad(t\ge0).$$
Clause (a) includes $M=0$ and every real $\eta_0$, including zero. Clauses (b)-(e) concern the normalized law when $M\ne0$; no nonzero assumption on $\eta_0$ is required. Then:

(a) (factorisation) for every $t>0$ and almost every $k\in\mathbb R^{3}$,
$$|A_{b}(k,t)|^{2}=\eta_{0}^{2}\,t\,K_{t}\bigl(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta\bigr) \|M(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2},$$
and consequently
$\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^{2}=\eta_{0}^{2}t\int_{\mathbb R}
K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)$;

(b) (normalisation) if $M\ne0$, then for every $t>0$ the denominator
$\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)$ is finite and strictly positive,
so
$$P_{t}(B):=\frac{\int_{B}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)} {\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)}$$
defines a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R$ with
$P_{t}(\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda])=0$;

(c) (concentration) if $\nu_{b}=J_{b}\lambda$ for some $J_{b}\in
L^{1}(\lambda)$ with $J_{b}=0$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere on
$\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda]$, if $J_{b}$ is continuous at some $\Delta$ with
$0<\Delta<\Lambda$ and $J_{b}(\Delta)>0$, and if $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ is
continuous and bounded, then
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\int_{\mathbb R}f\,dP_{t}=f(\Delta);$$

(d) (positivity) if $\nu_{b}=J_{b}\lambda$ with $J_{b}\ge0$
$\lambda$-almost everywhere and $J_{b}>0$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere on a
Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ of positive Lebesgue measure, then
$P_{t}(B)>0$ for every $t>0$;

(e) (tail concentration) under the hypotheses of (c), for every $\delta>0$,
$\lim_{t\to\infty}P_{t}\bigl(\{E:|E-\Delta|\ge\delta\}\bigr)=0$.

No dynamics, transition probability, rate, decay or physical identification is
asserted; the lemma computes an explicit kernel, its normalised push-forward
law and that law's limit.

all_current_steps.quote: 1.1 [The first Dyson term in the one-photon sector at level $b$] By [F1] and [F2], $\Psi_1(t)=-(i/\hbar)\int_0^tV(s)\Psi_0\,ds$ with $V(s)=e^{isH_0/\hbar}Be^{-isH_0/\hbar}$. The free initial phase is $e^{-isH_0/\hbar}\Psi_0=e^{-isE_a/\hbar}\Psi_0$, and $B\Psi_0=\eta_0\sum_jD_j^Wv_a\otimes g_j$. In the linear-first convention, the coefficient of $v_b$ in $e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^Wv_a$ is $\langle e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^Wv_a,v_b\rangle=e^{isE_b/\hbar}c_j$ by [F3]. Consequently $Q_bV(s)\Psi_0=v_b\otimes\eta_0 e^{-is\Delta/\hbar}e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M$. The bounded projection passes through the vector integral, giving $Q_b\Psi_1(t)=v_b\otimes[-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M\,ds]=v_b\otimes A_b(\cdot,t)$ by the definition of $A_b$. Equivalently, for every $f\in\mathfrak h$, $\langle\Psi_1(t),v_b\otimes f\rangle=\langle A_b(\cdot,t),f\rangle$, with all coefficients in the linear first slot. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F7, algebra]

2.1 [The coefficient] Clause (a) of [[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] with $t>0$ gives $\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^{2}=\eta_{0}^{2}t\int K_{t}(E-\Delta)d\nu_{b}(E)$, which is $\gamma_{b}(t)$. This proves (a). [F5, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 [Absorption mirror] For a unit $g\in\mathfrak h$, the first Dyson term with initial vector $\Phi_0=v_b\otimes g$ is well defined as a norm integral: the free evolution preserves the one-photon sector, and the creation/contraction bounds [F1] bound each vertex uniformly from that sector to the vacuum plus two-photon sectors. The sector maps are bounded and free evolution is strongly continuous, giving a norm-continuous integrand; these sector formulas supply the extension even when $g\notin D(\varepsilon)$. No full Dyson-series assertion for this initial vector is used. Set $h_s=e^{-is\varepsilon/\hbar}g$. The vacuum component of $\phi(g_j)h_s$ is $\langle h_s,g_j\rangle\Omega$ in the linear-first convention. The coefficient of $v_a$ in $e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^Wv_b$ is $e^{isE_a/\hbar}\overline{c_j}$ by [F3]; thus $\langle V(s)\Phi_0,v_a\otimes\Omega\rangle=\eta_0e^{is\Delta/\hbar}\sum_j\overline{c_j}\langle h_s,g_j\rangle=\eta_0e^{is\Delta/\hbar}\overline{\langle M,h_s\rangle}$. Integrating with $-i/\hbar$ in the first slot gives the displayed absorption amplitude. Step 1.1 and unitarity give $\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}=-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}\langle e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M,g\rangle ds=-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}\langle M,h_s\rangle ds$. Since $\eta_0$ is real, conjugating this scalar integral proves $\alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}=-\overline{\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}}$ and equal moduli, including $t=0$ or $\eta_0=0$. This proves (c) for the full complex couplings. [F1, F3, F4, F7, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Exact projection probability] Since $H_{0}$ commutes with $Q_{b}$ (both are diagonal in the level basis and $\Pi_1$ is the degree-one Fock-sector projection and the free field group preserves every particle-number sector, [F1], [F4]), [F2] gives $Q_{b}e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}=Q_{b}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\Psi(t)=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}Q_{b}\Psi(t)$, so $\|Q_{b}e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}\|=\|Q_{b}\Psi(t)\|$ by unitarity. 4.1 [Scope and assembly] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a), step 3.1 proves (b) and step 2.2 proves (c). Adopt the model, the declared upward level pair $(a,b)$ and the page data
$c_{j},M,\nu_{b},A_{b}$ of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]] and
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]], and the
single-vertex emission coefficient $\gamma_{b}(t)$ of
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-emission-and-absorption-coefficients]]
clause (a). Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the density hypothesis:
$\nu_{b}=J_{b}\lambda$ for some $J_{b}\in L^{1}(\lambda)$ with $J_{b}=0$
$\lambda$-almost everywhere on $\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda]$, continuous at
$\Delta$. Then:

(a) (resonant limit) if $0<\Delta<\Lambda$ and $J_{b}(\Delta)>0$, then
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\gamma_{b}(t)}{t} =\frac{2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}}{\hbar}\,J_{b}(\Delta);$$

(b) (above-cutoff limit) if $\Delta>\Lambda$, then
$\lim_{t\to\infty}\gamma_{b}(t)/t=0$; the boundary case $\Delta=\Lambda$ is not
asserted;

(c) (rate reading) the theorem declares the **model rate coefficient**
$$\Gamma_{b}:=\frac{2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}}{\hbar}\,J_{b}(\Delta) \qquad(0<\Delta<\Lambda),$$
read in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ by the unit convention of the model (the interaction
term is read in joules), as the model's reading of the limit in (a); the
identification of the mode density $J_{b}$, the cutoff $\Lambda$ or the
coupling $\eta_{0}$ with laboratory data is a tested identification with
uncertainty under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]);

(d) (scope) clauses (a)-(c) concern the limit of the explicit single-vertex
coefficient per unit time. They assert no exact exponential decay of any
population, no lifetime or linewidth, no weak-coupling, Markov or
environmental property of the model's exact evolution, no all-time validity of
a rate law and no measured rate; in particular $\Gamma_{b}$ is a property of
the declared model together with its declared mode density, not an observed
decay constant.

step_quotes.quote: 1.1 [Resonant limit] By [F1], $\gamma_{b}(t)/t=\eta_{0}^{2}\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)d\nu_{b}(E)$ for $t>0$; substituting the density $J_{b}$ by [F3] and applying the first case of [F2] gives $\lim_{t}\gamma_{b}(t)/t=\eta_{0}^{2}\cdot\frac{2\pi}{\hbar}J_{b}(\Delta)$. This is (a). [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

## Statement

Adopt the prescribed dipole-drive model of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-dipole-drive-and-long-wavelength]] with its
matter data $W\simeq\mathbb C^{d}$, $H_{a}$, $D^{W}_{1},D^{W}_{2},D^{W}_{3}$ and
its compact interval $I=[t_{0},t_{1}]$, the driven model of
[[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] clause (b)(i) and the
framework readings of P1, P2 and P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Assume the Axioms of
Countable Choice and of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $v_{i},v_{k}$ be orthonormal eigenvectors of
$H_{a}$ with $H_{a}v_{i}=E_{i}v_{i}$, $H_{a}v_{k}=E_{k}v_{k}$, put
$\Delta:=E_{k}-E_{i}$, take $s,t\in I$ with $s\le t$, put $\tau:=t-s$ and let
$A_{ki}(t,s)=e^{iE_k\tau/\hbar}\langle U(t,s)v_{i},v_{k}\rangle$ be the
model's transition amplitude of clause (e) of the driven model with
$U(t,s)$ the propagator of the drive family
$H_{\mathrm d}(r)=H_{a}-\sum_{j}E_{\mathrm{ext},j}(r)D^{W}_{j}$. Then:

(a) (first-order amplitude and remainder) with
$$A^{(1)}_{ki}(t,s)=\frac{i}{\hbar}\sum_{j=1}^{3}\int_{s}^{t} e^{i\Delta(r-s)/\hbar}\,E_{\mathrm{ext},j}(r)\, \bigl\langle D^{W}_{j}v_{i},v_{k}\bigr\rangle\,dr,$$
one has $A_{ki}(t,s)=\delta_{ik}+A^{(1)}_{ki}(t,s)+R_{ki}(t,s)$ with
$|R_{ki}(t,s)|\le e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{2}/2$, where
$K:=\sup_{r\in I}\|V(r)\|/\hbar$ with $V(r):=-\sum_jE_{\mathrm{ext},j}(r)D_j^W$; in particular the first-order
amplitude is the model's exact amplitude up to the displayed Dyson remainder;

(b) (monochromatic co- and counter-rotating terms) if
$\mathbf E_{\mathrm{ext}}(r)=\mathbf E_{0}\cos(\omega r+\vartheta)$ with
$\mathbf E_{0}\in\mathbb R^{3}$, $\omega,\vartheta\in\mathbb R$ and
$W:=-\sum_{j}E_{0,j}D^{W}_{j}$ (a bounded self-adjoint operator on $W$), then
$V(r)=W\cos(\omega r+\vartheta)$ and
$$A^{(1)}_{ki}=a_{+}+a_{-},\qquad a_{\pm}=-\frac{i}{2\hbar}\bigl\langle Wv_{i},v_{k}\bigr\rangle e^{\mp i\vartheta_{0}}\frac{e^{i(\Delta\mp\hbar\omega)\tau/\hbar}-1} {i(\Delta\mp\hbar\omega)/\hbar},\qquad \vartheta_{0}:=\omega s+\vartheta,$$
with the value $\tau$ for the quotient when $\Delta\mp\hbar\omega=0$;
consequently the co-rotating term satisfies
$$|a_{+}|=\bigl|\bigl\langle Wv_{i},v_{k}\bigr\rangle\bigr|\, \frac{\bigl|\sin\bigl((\Delta-\hbar\omega)\tau/(2\hbar)\bigr)\bigr|} {|\Delta-\hbar\omega|} \quad(\Delta\ne\hbar\omega),\qquad |a_{+}|=\bigl|\bigl\langle Wv_{i},v_{k}\bigr\rangle\bigr|\frac{\tau}{2\hbar} \quad(\Delta=\hbar\omega),$$
and the counter-rotating term satisfies
$|a_{-}|\le|\langle Wv_{i},v_{k}\rangle|/|\Delta+\hbar\omega|$ whenever
$\Delta+\hbar\omega\ne0$;

(c) (equal stimulated coefficients) for the two-level case $d=2$ with
orthonormal eigenvectors $v_{\uparrow},v_{\downarrow}$, $H_av_{\uparrow}
=E_{\uparrow}v_{\uparrow}$, $H_av_{\downarrow}=E_{\downarrow}v_{\downarrow}$
and $\Delta=E_{\uparrow}-E_{\downarrow}>0$, the actual upward and downward
first-order amplitudes under the same real prescribed field obey
$$A^{(1)}_{\downarrow\uparrow}(t,s)=-\overline{A^{(1)}_{\uparrow\downarrow}(t,s)}.$$
In particular their squared moduli, the model's first-order stimulated
emission and absorption coefficients, are equal. For the monochromatic
field of (b), the upward co-rotating component at detuning
$\Delta-\hbar\omega$ and the reverse downward component at the opposite
detuning $\hbar\omega-\Delta$ have equal moduli as well; reversing the
transition conjugates its matrix element and swaps the two exponential
components, with the same overall minus-conjugation relation;

(d) (exact two-level identifications) if $d=2$ with the orthonormal basis
$(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$ and the Pauli matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e), if
$$H_{a}=\frac{\hbar\omega_{0}}{2}\sigma_{z},\qquad D^{W}_{1}=d\,\sigma_{x},\qquad D^{W}_{2}=d\,\sigma_{y},\qquad D^{W}_{3}=0$$
for some real $d$ of unit $\mathrm{C\,m}$, and if the prescribed field is
$\mathbf E_{\mathrm{ext}}(r)=E_{0}(\cos(\omega r),\sin(\omega r),0)$ with
$E_{0}\in\mathbb R$, then $H_{\mathrm d}(r)$ is exactly the declared circular
two-level drive model of clause (f) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]]
with transverse coupling $\Omega_{1}:=-2dE_{0}/\hbar$, so the exact Rabi
populations of [[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-circular-drive-exact-rabi]] clause
(b) are the model's level populations; if instead
$\mathbf E_{\mathrm{ext}}(r)=E_{0}(\cos(\omega r),0,0)$ and $D^{W}_{1}=d\sigma_{x}$,
$D^{W}_{2}=D^{W}_{3}=0$, then $H_{\mathrm d}(r)$ is the declared **linear**
two-level drive model with the same $\Omega_{1}$ and the rotating-wave error
contract of [[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-linear-drive-rotating-wave-error]]
clauses (b),(c) applies to it when $\omega\ne0$. For $\omega=0$ the linear model is the constant Hamiltonian $H_*=(\hbar/2)(\omega_0\sigma_z+\Omega_1\sigma_x)$ with exact propagator $\cos(q\tau/2)I-i\sin(q\tau/2)(\omega_0\sigma_z+\Omega_1\sigma_x)/q$ for $q=\sqrt{\omega_0^2+\Omega_1^2}>0$, and $I$ when $q=0$;

(e) (scope) clauses (a)-(d) concern the prescribed classical drive model. The
field is unaffected by the matter's transitions; the model contains no
quantized field, no photon number and no vacuum, so no spontaneous emission,
no emission rate and no photon count is supplied by it. The identifications of
$H_{a},D^{W}_{j},d,\mathbf E_{\mathrm{ext}}$ with a laboratory atom and field
and of the initial preparation with an eigenvector of $H_{a}$ are tested
identifications with uncertainty under P7, and no value of $\omega_{0}$, $d$,
$E_{0}$, $\omega$ or $\Omega_{1}$ is asserted.
